subject: SLA: response matrix, service credits & blackout scheduling
messages:
From: Claire Hughes <claire.hughes@clearbank.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-05T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Questions on SLA redlines and blackout windows

Rishi,

Thanks for sending the draft order form and SLA redlines. Procurement and our infra team reviewed and surfaced a few specific asks before we can move to legal: 

- Uptime target: you have 99.95% at monthly granularity. Can you confirm how that maps to per-region availability (we operate EU + US production pods)?
- Service credit: the formula in section 4.2 uses a linear slab that scales with minutes down. We need to understand worst-case cap and whether credits stack with emergency maintenance.
- Response matrix: we prefer a P0 < 1 hour ack / 4 hour remediation window for production incidents — the draft shows 2h/8h. Any flexibility here?
- Scheduled maintenance blackout: our change windows (weekly deploys) are Tuesday 02:00–04:00 UTC and Friday 03:00–05:00 UTC. Can Redwood guarantee no scheduled rolling upgrades inside those windows for our tenant, or provide firm blackout carveouts?

I've attached our team's annotated PDF (ClearBank_SLA_comments_v1.pdf). If helpful, I can set up a short call with infra next week.

Best,
Claire Hughes
Senior SRE — ClearBank
procurement@clearbank.com
Attachment: ClearBank_SLA_comments_v1.pdf (annotation summary)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Claire Hughes <claire.hughes@clearbank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-06T11:04:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on SLA redlines and blackout windows

Claire — thanks, and appreciated the clear notes. Looping Laura (product/legal owner for order form) and Aditya (ops lead) to get precise answers and a counterproposal.

High level responses:
- Multi-region mapping: our hosted offering measures availability at the region-level and at the global account level. We can commit to 99.95% per region for dedicated accounts on a 30‑day rolling window, provided the order form lists both regions explicitly.
- Credits cap: current draft caps credits at 50% of the monthly bill. We can propose a scaled cap: 25% cap up to 4 hours downtime, 50% cap for >4h events that are platform-wide. We do not stack credits for emergency maintenance vs unplanned downtime; we pay whichever is applicable.
- Response/Remediation: Aditya — can you confirm ops SLA capability to aim for 1h ack / 4h remediation for P0 for ClearBank given their 24x7 criticality?
- Blackout carveouts: Laura — legal asked whether ops guarantees can be operational (config flags) or need contractual blackout exclusions. For now, ops can honor requested tenant blackout windows for scheduled maintenance if we add them to the order form; emergencies still may require short, pre-notified interventions.

I'll compile a redline and a short memo with the tradeoffs. Planning to send the counterproposal by Monday EOD.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_SLA_counter_v2.docx (outline of proposed credit caps & response ladder)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-07T09:23:00-05:00
Subject: Internal: ClearBank SLA items (notes)

Team — quick internal notes to shape Rishi's reply.

- Region commitments: we should avoid promising "per-region" uptime for self-managed/private installs. For hosted (what ClearBank is procuring) we can commit per-region 99.95 but add a clause: if ClearBank requests region‑exclusive capacity (pinning), we need a 14‑day lead time and additional cost.
- Credits: propose the staircase cap Rishi suggested. Add explicit exclusions for (a) customer misconfig, (b) scheduled maintenance with >=72h notice unless it's outside blackout windows.
- Response times: ops can meet 1h ack for P0 if we classify ClearBank P0 incidents as "customer-critical" in the order form; remediation SLAs tied to complexity tiers (app-level vs infra-level). Recommend: P0 ack 1h, P0 remediation target 4h (best-effort incl. third-party).
- Blackouts: to be conservative contractually: allow ops to request "emergency window" for security patches but require 24h notice where possible and guaranteed scheduling outside customer blackout unless the fix is CVE critical.

I'll add a short paragraph for negotiation leverage: we can offer a 30% first-year credit uplift instead of lowering availability target — helps pricing and risk.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Contracts — Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Claire Hughes <claire.hughes@clearbank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-11-09T16:43:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on SLA redlines and blackout windows

Claire — following internal review (see cc), here's a concise counterproposal for ClearBank to take to legal/procurement: 

1) Availability
- Commitment: 99.95% per-region (US, EU) measured on a rolling 30-day window for Redwood hosted service.
- If ClearBank requires region-exclusive pinned capacity, include a provisioning lead time of 14 days and an incremental fee (to be listed on the order form).

2) Service credit formula & caps
- Stairs: 0–60 minutes: 5% credit; 61–240 minutes: 15% credit; 241–480 minutes: 30% credit; >480 minutes: 50% credit of the monthly service fee attributable to the impacted region.
- Cap: maximum credit 50% of monthly fee. Credits do not stack; the single highest applicable credit applies.
- Exclusions: (i) Customer misconfiguration or third-party dependent outages; (ii) Scheduled maintenance with >=72h notice unless scheduled during customer blackout; (iii) Force majeure.

3) Response & remediation
- P0: 1 hour acknowledgement; 4 hour remediation target (customer‑critical incidents).
- P1: 2 hour acknowledgement; 12 hour remediation target.
- Remediation targets are "target" (best-effort) with root cause and follow-up timelines in the incident report. Contractual remedies remain credit-based.

4) Scheduled maintenance & blackout windows
- Redwood will respect ClearBank's weekly blackout windows (Tuesday 02:00–04:00 UTC and Friday 03:00–05:00 UTC) for scheduled rolling upgrades for tenant-scoped maintenance, provided ClearBank lists these in the order form.
- Emergency security patches: Redwood reserves the right to apply critical CVE patches inside blackout windows with 24h notice where practicable; if immediate action is required to mitigate active exploitation, Redwood will notify and coordinate and credits/exclusions will follow the above exclusions.

5) Next steps
- Attached: Redwood_SLA_counter_v2.docx with redline markup and clause language snippets.
- If this looks reasonable, would you like an annotated doc we can hand to ClearBank legal, or do you prefer a short 30-min sync to walk through tradeoffs?

Appreciate the collaboration — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
